lessons.title: Sounds and Greetings
lessons.objective: Say jobsite words clearly and greet your crew and coworkers in Spanish.
lessons.focus: The five vowels, ch, j, ll, rr and the written accent in tool names; greetings

words.note: Spanish vowels are short and pure: a as in 'father', o as in 'more'.
ch sounds like English 'church'.
j is a strong breathy h: HEH-feh. For a woman: la jefa.
ll sounds like English y in Mexico: YAH-veh. Also means key or faucet.
rr is a rolled r; ll sounds like y: ca-rre-TI-ya.
Stress falls on -ti-: mar-TI-yo.
A single r between vowels is a quick tap, like the dd in 'ladder'.
Stress on -da-: an-DA-mio.
The written accent marks the stressed syllable: ca-MIÓN.
b after a vowel is soft, with the lips barely touching: O-bra.
Formal. With a coworker you know well: ¿Cómo estás?

words.en: How do you say "hard hat" in Spanish?

lessons.speaking: Greet a crew member, say your name, and ask how to say a tool in Spanish, then repeat the tool name clearly.

lessons.title: Numbers, Time and Measurements
lessons.objective: Give start times, counts and lengths in feet and inches for boards, bags and concrete.
lessons.focus: Numbers 0 to 1,000, clock time, and feet, inches, pounds and yards on site

words.note: Plural pies: 8 pies = 8 feet.
Concrete is ordered in yardas cúbicas (cubic yards).
Many crews just say la cinta.

words.en: We start at 7 in the morning.
words.es: Empezamos a las 7 de la mañana.

words.note: Use de for a measurement: tablas de 8 pies.

words.es: La pared mide 10 pies y 6 pulgadas.

words.en: The truck is bringing 9 yards of concrete.
words.es: El camión trae 9 yardas de concreto.

words.en: Each bag weighs 94 pounds, according to the label.
words.es: Cada saco pesa 94 libras, según la etiqueta.

lessons.speaking: Tell a crew member what time the crew starts and stops, and read them the length of 3 boards in feet and inches.

lessons.title: Ser and Estar
lessons.objective: Say who people are on site and describe what is broken, loose, level or dry.
lessons.focus: ser for what something or someone is, estar for its condition or location

words.note: For a woman: la carpintera.
Same word for a woman, with la: la electricista.
rota with feminine nouns: la escalera está rota.
Concreto fresco is concrete that has not set.

words.en: I'm the foreman on this job.
words.es: Soy el mayordomo de esta obra.
words.note: Mayordomo is common on US jobsites; capataz is also used. ser: who you are.

words.en: He's a carpenter and she's an electrician.
words.es: Él es carpintero y ella es electricista.
words.note: No un or una after ser for a job.
estar: a condition that can change.

words.en: The tools are in the truck.
words.es: Las herramientas están en la troca.
words.note: estar for location. Troca is common US Spanish for pickup truck.

lessons.speaking: Describe the site to a crew member: say who each worker is and whether the scaffold, the wall and the concrete are loose, level or dry.
